//: Fixes that must be present in any release, expressed as behaviour rather than as commit ids. A cherry-pick across sixteen releases produces a new SHA, so an ancestry check would fail on a correct port and pass on a stale branch that happens to share history. Each entry names a file, a pattern that proves the behaviour, and why it must not be lost.

required.why: The pairing flow and the account-connection flow must record the same facts. Without one constructor they drifted, and a paired vault told its owner to re-pair — which minted a second host row.

required.pattern: a paired vault is never told to re-pair
required.why: The behaviour is only as durable as the assertion that pins it.
The confirmation must record the account the server verified, not one the host chose.
The packaged bundle must carry what the relay refuses without; source that passes is not an artefact that works.
